sents.t: I have a driver’s license from my country, but it isn’t good here, so I have to get an American license.
Carlos offered to teach me.
“I’m a math teacher,” he joked.
“I’m very patient.”
On Saturday morning, we drove to the empty parking lot behind the high school.
I sat in the driver’s seat of Carlos’s old blue car.
My hands were shaking.
“First, check your mirrors. Put on your seat belt. Now, slowly push the gas pedal,” Carlos said.
The car jumped forward!
I hit the brake too hard, and Carlos’s coffee spilled on his jacket.
While I was practicing, it started to snow lightly.
We practiced turning, parking, and stopping at stop signs.
In America, people drive on the right side of the road.
That was new for me too.
After two hours, I was driving much more carefully.
On the way home, Carlos let me drive on a real street.
A police car was driving behind us the whole time!
I was very nervous, but I didn’t make any mistakes.
“Good job,” Carlos said.
“Next stop: the DMV!”
